about: What the loading card shows after an update (#745): per release, newest first, up to five short player-facing lines. Written by tools/release/whats-new.mjs.

lines: Outdoor skies follow the clock, with stars at night.
Read, answer and close your bug reports on the website too, under Community's Support.
Drag a machine you've set down to slide it along the floor, right up next to another.
Eight more reactions to pick from: 👏 😊 🤔 😍 🔥 👀 😅 and 💯.
What's new in the Menu shows every version, with ‹ › or the arrow keys to step through them.
Walk onto a crack or Manhole rug on an upper floor of your house and you drop to the floor below.
Decoration Mode scrolls into the back yard, so you can pick up and move what lies there.
Things dragged from your pack land where you let go in your back yard.
The Bureaucratic Hall has its eight waiting chairs, and you stand on its floor again.
Prices read the number then ₡ everywhere: shops, vendors, storage, mail and auctions.
A window left open on a laptop that went to sleep no longer takes your character back when it wakes.
A machine that can't go down because you stand too close to the others now says so.
Something that ended up under the house floor comes back up onto it.
Visiting Stones on East Spice and four other streets stand at their street's end again.
A long description in an item's menu no longer squeezes its actions into a few rows.
Archimedes Acres's Group Hall has its own street for its group's members.
Drinks at the Pot Luck Day feast offer Drink, and drinking them works.
On a computer, only things in reach glow under the mouse, as in Glitch.
Progress Way's camera pan to the Street Spirit works, as in Glitch.
The Map's home card has House and Tower buttons beside Home.
Doors on the street map show what they are: a dino, a portal or a door.
The energy and mood rings change colour as they empty, as Glitch's gauges did.
Apple a Day gives its +5 energy when it ends, and every buff's end effect lands.
Croaking Piggies keep their own minute instead of all croaking as you arrive.
The teleporters on Ain't That Dry, Chiti Tiga and Harrisa Hara work again.
The secret passage behind the trunk in Koulato Cluster takes you to Ruta Asuncion again.
Open water and deep shafts no longer stop you on an invisible floor: you sink to the bottom.
Notes played on Piano Party's keys and stars are heard by everyone on the street.
Players' names are coloured in chat and in speech bubbles, one colour each.
Walking up to your house or pointing at it no longer makes the world blink out or go blank.
The glow around Helga and other vendors stays on their body through every animation.
Giant Icons can be placed at home, and visitors can Ruminate, Revere, Reflect and Tithe.
One click or tap on a garden plot does its job: harvest, hoe, water or fertilize.
A group's administrator can rename the group and change its description.
Coming back to the game from another page reconnects it, so chat and shared actions work again.
On a computer, things in reach glow, as in Glitch, instead of a label following you.
Only the owner, key holders and visitors let in can see inside a house and its back yard, as in Glitch.
Those inside can dig a back yard's Dirt Piles and work its Peat Bogs, shared with the owner.
When the owner logs off, visitors without a key are walked out to the front door.
The Game Show ticket's spinning wheel draws in front of barnacles.
Camera Mode at your own home can snap the whole house, Tower or home street, every floor stacked.
On a computer, sound keeps playing when you switch tabs, with a setting to choose.
Playing a musicblock for someone shows its bubble over them and gives them the block and notes.
Wall pieces go as high as Glitch allowed.
A visitor sees every Dirt Pile, Peat Bog and Patch in a friend's back yard.
Expand opens Glitch's dialog: what the next segment costs, what you have, and a button to use them.
Visitors see the owner's own house style.
A dead connection is found in seconds and says "Reconnecting...".
A Subway ticket plays the teleport chime, and stations play their region's music.
A gem found while mining shows in the activity log.
Butterflies and Batterflies wander their whole street at random, and everyone sees them in the same place.
Your first shrine donation offers Respect for the Beginnings again.
Show the way never sends you through a locked door you have no key for.
Music and sounds pause while you are in another app or tab, and pick up where they left off.
Firebog street spirits' flames flicker and their vines sway.
A room holds any number of furniture pieces, as in Glitch, and visitors see every one.
Sparkly of Interest shows its count on each step and finishes at 100.
A quest's place link opens the Map on the way into its region, with a Show the way button.
Quest steps read as words, not the quest editor's placeholders.
The Vine Radio: play 6 tunes for the Music Crabs and get a radio for your home street.
Sorted bags show a small badge with what they are sorted for.
The Bookcase can be made again on the Construction Tool.
Machines and the Crafty Bot work on every floor of your house, as in Glitch.
Encyclopedia How do I guides give short answers to questions players asked.
Encyclopedia search finds what each page says, not only its name, and shows what matched.
Street lists: every street with a community garden, a shrine to each Giant, a vendor, a subway and more.
On a phone at home, Decorate, Cultivate and Change Style have their own row under your home's name.
On a phone, your house and Tower floors fill the screen.
In the upright iPhone Home Screen app, the street runs up to the top bar again.
Snaps are taken at full screen size and open in a full-screen viewer with Previous and Next.
Snaps stay private until you make one public; public ones show on your profile.
Piles in your house and on your Tower floors, shelves and tables have no stack limit.
Home street music changes with the street style, as in Glitch.
The Game Show wheel can be spun the moment it appears.
A quiet release: behind-the-scenes work for the game's administrators.
Things you drop, drag or set down in your house show at once instead of after a pause.
Emblems and other one-to-a-stack things pile up on your house floor, shelves and tables.
Things you set on your house or Tower floor are for everyone there again, as in Glitch.
Moving one of your locked things onto the floor unlocks it.
You can move floor stacks along the floor in Decoration Mode.
Teleporting works while visiting someone else's home street, house or Tower.
House and Tower floors hold as many things as you like.
The Bureaucratic Hall has its office again, with the lizard at his computer.
Dino and subway entrances show on the street map and the loading picture.
The phone page has an Account tab: email, password, Change name and your profile description.
Marylpole Mount Quarter: claim a free house lot, and your house stands there for everyone to visit.
From December 26 the Toy Vendor sells Confetti Poppers, and the whole street sees the confetti.
Make Bubbly with a Cocktail Shaker and Toast with the players around you.
At a Groddle midnight on December 31, earn a Midnight Sparkly and the "Rang In the New Ur" badge.
Every quest Tiny Speck wrote but never shipped has an Encyclopedia page.
A new phone layout: four fixed buttons at the top right, and the Map fills the screen.
On a phone, bags, Social, Quests and the Menu lift the street so your Glitch stays in view.
The Encyclopedia has one page per rock, peat bog and tree, each listing every street that has one.
Long chat lines in Global, Help, Trade, groups and IMs show in full.
A mined-out rock is gone until it reforms, as in Glitch, instead of leaving a faint ghost.
Change your character's name in Menu, Account: 1,000 currants, once every 30 days.
New characters and sign-ups work again after a spam filter had been turning them away.
A full bag's backdrop in the pack row is a soft grey instead of jet black.
Things dropped on a house floor, back yard or Tower floor are shared: everyone inside can pick them up.
Happy New Ur: a countdown and fireworks at each of the six Groddle midnights on December 31.
Drag a stack from the pack onto the street to drop it at your feet.
Character names can be two letters long, and animal names keep periods, so Dr. Oink stays Dr. Oink.
Encyclopedia pages for dirt piles, peat bogs, trees, rocks and animals list the streets that have them.
On a phone, the Decorate and Cultivate rows scroll with a sideways swipe; pull a tile up to place it.
Customize your house docks at the bottom and the street zooms out so you can see your house.
On the Map, streets being built are a blue road with a road-works sign.
The Bureaucracy clerks sell Card-Carrying Qualifications to badge holders too.
A Pot Luck Day Chicken dressed in one costume can be re-dressed in the other.
Streets look as they did in 2012, checked against players' old snaps and screenshots.
Clouds, mist and fog stay soft and see-through, and signposts no longer glow on dark streets.
Symphonious Maximus and the missing floor are rebuilt to match their 2012 screenshots.
Each Ticket to Paradise course has its own sky, and Cloud Rings has hoops that turn gold.
The Greedy Street Spirit's exit takes you back, and warns you first if you missed part of the story.
A Door can be restyled: all 32 Door styles from the original, with Upgrade and Change Style.
Furniture stands at its own depth, as in the original: beds against the back wall, rugs on the walking line.
A trip that fails to load tries once more, then leaves you where you were and says so.
A street spirit with two projects offers the one you are helping with first.
An upright iPhone shows the game's dark in the status bar instead of a light fog.
Choose your house: all ten original houses, every part customizable from the house door's menu, free.
Eight wallpapers, floors and ceilings made for the original but never sold are in Decorate.
Start a party from Storyland, Paradise, Winter Walk and more, and come back to the spot you left.
The subway train's map looks like the Map's Subway view, and each line has its own colour.
Circle the spot on a report's picture with up to three rings.
A Calendar of Ur's holidays, the events coming up and the Feats, opens from the clock.
Radial Heights runs its own scripts: stars light as you touch them, and touching them in order has an ending.
Pumpkin Seeds plant during Pot Luck Day as well as Zilloween, in a crop bed or an herb bed.
Your Butler tells you when the Rook is attacking a street.
iPhone and iPad Safari show a tip that Add to Home Screen plays the game full screen.
Leaving the Greedy Street Spirit story early no longer leaves the quest stuck: a Piggy offers it again.
Street project work keeps going when a unit arrives a little early.
On an upright phone the top bar shortens your counts (70K, 1.3K) instead of cutting them off.
In Decorate, moving an item onto a matching stack joins them, on shelves too.
Hellish Grapes lie in random piles again, and one squish still takes one bunch.
Pot Luck Day begins November 22, with a card when it starts and another on Thanksgiving Day.
The Harvest Table and feast appear at midnight for players already at Groddle Forest Junction.
Groddle Originals, a new page for everything made for Groddle that Glitch never had.
Quick Act presses on a street tree no longer choose Talk to.
An upgraded street shows its upgrade after a login or reload online.
Mining while other players use tools nearby no longer freezes your character.
Narrow streets fill the window instead of showing black bars at the sides.
Garden signs and other street signs show their words.
The street card on arrival lists the Batterflies on every street that has them.
The Shrine window shows each Giant's emblem and links the Giant's Encyclopedia page.
The start card shows a returning player today's skill, Feat, a tip and a nudge toward a badge.
Help mine, Cubimal races, battles and chat work inside a Party Space.
Vendors near you show an icon for each store.
Holding Enter at a vendor no longer buys the same thing again and again.
Under a ladder out of reach, the game tells you to jump, then press Up in the air.
Quoins in Paradise, A Summer's Day and Penumbra pay your quoin multiplier, as in Glitch.
Refuel asks how many Fuel Cells to put in before any are used.
Each stat has one icon and colour everywhere, from the top bar to reward screens.
The Giants list, the favor chip and the shrine window show each Giant's own shrine symbol.
Street Spirits and mailboxes no longer stand inside a tree's crown.
Every street's loading card now shows a picture of the street: 1,474 streets, up from 82.
Street pictures no longer leave out decorations.
Every Patch in your yard is drawn, not just the first eight.
A friend's garden help can no longer turn a ripe crop back into seeds.
Following a friend no longer takes you onto a street still being built.
Inside the subway car, your star moves along the line map during the ride.
After arriving by a signpost or door, /stuck takes you back to where you came in.
The subway route card names the line to board, the stop to get off at and the steps up.
Fruit trees and the other trants show how much they hold: bare, half or full.
Your own Glitch appears in your own look when the game starts.
You walk up a subway station's steps to the entrance.
A vendor, a trade or a letter never takes a bag that still holds things.
Online, other players can mourn or celebrate your grave once, as in Glitch.
Street changes are quicker, and a click on a door or subway steps goes straight through.
The map draws streets you have not been to as a dotted line, as Glitch did.
Vanity offers None for tops, trousers and shoes.
Pot's Empty Table and other event quests can be pinned.
The Contribute page's ledger shows the two newest sponsor gifts: three sponsors now.
The stack you drag is the one that goes, onto a display box, a Butler, a cabinet or a trade.
Trades, mail, auctions and home sales go through while the game is saving.
Race Tickets and teleport scripts work inside a Party Space, as in Glitch.
A broken part of the game no longer freezes your avatar.
Mined-out rocks take longer to come back, so you work a street's rocks instead of two in turn.
Visitors can keep petting, watering and harvesting on a home street after half an hour there.
Towers and Note Poles stand where Glitch drew them, so you no longer float above the porch.
The Jellisac Mound grows three Jellisacs.
An expired Party Space sends you back where you entered it, not to Baqala.
Reports in the game show the chat's emoji reactions, and you can add your own.
Spinning, smelting and crushing take as much as the pack holds, so Spin Doctor can be earned.
Encyclopedia item pages say how to get each item.
The subway's red button sits where the 2012 stations had it.
A display box offers every item it can take.
Music and sounds come back after you step away or the system interrupts them.
Short looping street music no longer plays twice at once in Safari.
Food can be dragged onto a Piggy Feeder, as in Glitch.
Thanksgiving Day's feast: the week's Harvest Table food is set out at Groddle Forest Junction.
The Harvest Table is three boards long, and Look lists every dish with who laid it.
Mining and digging together at a friend's home rocks and Dirt Piles count as helping.
Map routes ride the subway when it saves more than about five streets of walking.
Wine of the Dead flies from Hell's Bartender into your pack, as in Glitch.
In a back yard, trees and pours stay on their own Patch after another Patch wears out.
Smuggling runs only send you where you can walk, and never by subway.
Sky no longer shows below the ground when the camera is low on a street.
Musicblocks can be played in Hell, as in Glitch.
Pot Luck Day (Nov 22-29), the first festival made for Groddle: dress a street Chicken.
Lay a dish or a crop on the Harvest Table by the Groddle Forest Junction signpost.
Pot's Empty Table quest, Harvest Stuffing and five new badges come with Pot Luck Day.
Drop a stack on a friend's Butler to leave it as a package, or on yours as a gift.
Mining swings take a third of Glitch's time: 6 seconds down to 2.4 for Mining I to IV.
Online, you see other players at work: a thought bubble shows their tool as they mine or dig.
On your home street, visitors see your harvests, furniture and decor as you do them.
The Outer Mind takes its 2012 shape, and Winter Haven's trees carry their snow.
Street gardens stand where players' 2012 pictures show them, with every bed Glitch had.
The loose Apples on every street are gone; Glitch never had them.
Phones: pinned quests are one round button in the top bar that shows progress as a ring.
A new sound setting lets your own music keep playing under the game's sound effects.
The Encyclopedia has a subway map page with every station and its next stops.
Hub Completist badges need every street of their hub; badges already earned stay.
Barnacles in Kalavana and Jethimadh hang on walls and tree legs where Glitch hung them.
A new game no longer starts in Hechey Track's treetops, but on the street's arrival point.
A teleport or summons plays your Glitch's own one-second animation, as in Glitch.
Petting, milking, squeezing and more show Tiny Speck's own effects to players around you.
Poured Alphabet Sauce is Tiny Speck's glowing column of drifting letters, not a red puddle.
Winter Walk's caption stands inside its hollow tree arch again.
Tower projects ask How many for each part, with a Max button, instead of adding all you carry.
The subway map fits an upright phone, and zooms and pans with fingers, wheel or buttons.
A party invite works from a quest room or puzzle: the room waits, with your run and quoins kept.
Leaving the party takes you back to the same spot in the room.
From a race or a game you can go too, but going gives the game up, as in Glitch.
Walk Toward the Light and Radiant Glare are drawn with new art made from players' 2012 pictures.
On some phones, speech bubbles no longer draw thin lines out to the middle of the screen.
A party invite accepted at home opens the teleporter there, as in Glitch.
Today's Feat keeps every quest you finish, even when a report can't be taken right away.
Signpost words use the game's own font, so they read clearly on phones.
The Butler's longer hints stay up long enough to read, and also go to Local chat.
Sloths are Tiny Speck's own painted sloth again, hiding in the leaves of their trees.
Knock on a sloth's Knocker to call it: it spits snails into your pack in rounds of 1 to 4.
Pack search lists every match under the search box, items in bags included.
Local chat lists everyone on your street, with how many players are online.
A street with no road back to Ur shows an EXIT sign to take you back to your last street.
Party Spaces drop Glitch's own party quoins, back 60 to 120 seconds after you take one.
The Map dims the names of streets you have not visited yet.
Phones: the touch stick climbs ladders, and the street sheet has a Map button.
Sound effects keep playing after many Acts in a row.
Ix Completist asks for all nine Ix streets; a badge already earned is kept.
Rocks, shrines, vendors, soil patches and animals no longer stand up in the trees.
Subway stations are laid out as in Glitch, with A Red Button on the gate box.
A walk along a route keeps going while you open the Map, chat, Quests or Skills.
A quest card counts every step of a quest, and Pinned Quests list each step left.
In the iPhone Home Screen app the Encyclopedia opens over the game.
The first tutorial screen says how to pull the chain, and the chain is easier to hit on a phone.
A reload in the Cloud Level puts you back on the cloud you reached.
A jump beside a ladder is a jump: Up gets on a ladder only on a fresh press.
Peatland Moors and 20 other streets get their missing ladder steps.
Phones no longer draw black boxes in a street's rock faces.
Reports carry up to four pictures: drop, paste, pick or take them in the game.
Friends can help build a Tower floor once its owner starts it at the Workbench.
Clicking your currants lists the nearest vendor of each kind, with Set as destination.
The Menu has an "I'm stuck" row, and every encyclopedia page has a search box.
Dropping a tool onto a Tinkertool repairs it.
Every region map is now Tiny Speck's own 2012 painting, restored: all 51 of 51.
Phones: tap Act again to pick the highlighted row, or drag on Act and lift to choose.
The Feat Completed card shows the Petrified Rock sharp, drawn from Tiny Speck's own art.
The Make window says how many of the thing you're making you already carry.
Visitors can plant, water and pick the gardens on another player's home street.
Fourteen more region maps are Tiny Speck's 2012 paintings again, 48 of 51 regions in all.
Number keys do emotes again: 1 surprised, 2 angry, 3 happy, 4 AFK.
Home rocks wear out after 40 mine-outs, not 40 swings.
Finding the nearest shrine no longer ends on a street under construction.
Five more region maps are Tiny Speck's 2012 paintings again, 34 regions in all.
Mining takes Glitch's time again, and the pick swings on the rock.
Add to Home Screen opens Groddle Afternoon full screen, as an app.
Speech bubbles on phones move smoothly instead of bouncing back and forth.
Join the Club's shut door can no longer be jumped over.
Karnata, Lida and Massadoe's maps are Tiny Speck's 2012 paintings again, 29 regions in all.
Capture is offered again for a Piggy in your own back yard after a capture there.
Le Misérable II's small doors let you through only once you are shrunk.
On a sideways phone, Jump stays clear of Social and the report window stays visible.
A resting street's signpost says when its next project opens.
Ten more region maps are Tiny Speck's 2012 paintings again, 26 regions in all.
A save that does not go in now says so at the top of the game and keeps trying.
Phones get an Act button beside Jump that talks to, reads or uses whatever is nearest.
The Meal Vendor and Helga no longer turn into black squares on some Android phones.
The Piggy capture limit no longer applies in your own house, yards or Tower.
Drifa and Firozi's maps are Tiny Speck's 2012 paintings again, sixteen in all.
The restored region maps lose the pale strips at their left and right edges.
Ten more region maps are Tiny Speck's 2012 paintings again, from Aranna to Choru.
260 shrines in sixteen more regions stand where Tiny Speck's 2012 street pictures show them.
Legalize It's application is made in a shared Bureaucratic Hall, with everyone else in it.
An Autumn Day plays its own music, looped.
A cabinet's storage window fits a small phone without scrolling sideways.
Groddle Meadow's 36 shrines stand where Tiny Speck's 2012 street pictures show them.
Shrines, trees, vendors and animals keep off the Peat Bogs, Jellisacs and Barnacles.
The Louise Pasture Villa's door stands in an apartment house instead of an open field.
Swoonerflies show their name when you hover or tap them.
An open bag no longer holds back a quest's award, so Gwendolyn's Task offers its second part.
The World map is sharp on Retina screens and phones, with Tiny Speck's own charts.
Groddle Meadow, Alakol, Groddle Forest and Andra's maps are Tiny Speck's 2012 paintings again.
Rocks, peat bogs and paper trees that hung above the ground now sit on it.
The Quests panel's Offered tab lists every new quest, with Accept and Not right now.
Scraping a barnacle, digging and cutting peat sound while you work.
The featured street project works online for everyone again.
The Magic Rock wears Glitch's full white rim on its cards.
On phones the street runs edge to edge, upright or sideways, clear of the notch.
The Map has a World view of Tiny Speck's own world map, and a Subway view of the twelve stations.
Lotha Harte's three icicles play their notes, and the right order lights the heart.
Breezy, EZ Cookin' and Talking 'bout Soil Appreciation get their practice streets back.
Winter Walk's big icicles fall and stand as pillars you can climb.
An iPhone no longer closes the game on the way into heavy streets such as Froughtful Fen.
Pinching to zoom keeps the street drawn the whole time, and zoomed in it draws sharper.
Make, the Map, Mail, Decoration Mode and many more windows fit an upright phone.
A Still works on the ground, as in Glitch: drop it, then Distill and Collect there.
On phones the top bar shows your currants and favor, and Camera Mode opens from the Menu.
Rocks, trees, Paper Trees and mailboxes stand where players' 2012 snaps show them.
Teleportation V summons a friend to where you stand.
Two players on one rock or node are both paid, and Ice Nubbins take Help scrape.
Street projects ask "How many?", pay every helper and show a top-ten leaderboard.
Phones get pinch to zoom, a pack row that scrolls and signposts that take a finger.
Alternate characters: one login holds up to three characters, one playing at a time.
Playable on phones, with touch controls, a lighter render and windows that fit either way up.
Sharper on Retina screens: homes, wallpaper, home-street houses, quest rooms and more.
An Apple gives 5 energy and no mood, as Glitch's did.
Logging in at 0 energy on a new game day refills you before anything can send you to Hell.
No more stuck players at the second tutorial bag, the smuggler's hole or the Ancestral Lands kick.
Quoins hang where players snapped them in 2012, each its own kind.
The newest arrow or A/D key you press steers, so a key the game thinks is held never freezes you.
Winter Walk motes pay Glitch's quoin amounts and can't be farmed by leaving.
Mail can carry what Glitch let you mail, such as CrabPod Headphones.
Ladders and ledges line up with their art on streets narrower than a wide window.
Mortar Barnacles sit on the walls where Glitch had them, placed from players' 2012 snaps.
Classic no longer resizes the game on hover, and the iMG count fits.
Classic's character builder takes the 2012 Vanity layout, with size sliders.
Classic Skills step one level at a time, with the 2012 study bar.
A busy save of project gifts and rewards no longer leads to a dropped connection.
Apple a Day's energy boost now shows when it lands, or says your energy was already full.
One featured street project at a time, shown under the street name and at the top of Projects.
Global announces the featured project when it opens and when it is built.
Feat goals grow with how many played the day before.
A full bag's bar turns the accent colour, so full never looks like almost full.
Yard plants step aside for a garden instead of poking through it.
Street Spirits give their street's project again: Talk to opens it.
Group Halls are built on their roped lot with its house-and-hammer sign.
The Incantations Feat works between real players: three of you on one street, one line each.
Plant asks which seed to use, and dropping a seed on a plot plants it.
Trophies stand on wall shelves, as they could in Glitch.
The gut streets drop you down to the way out instead of lifting you back up the gut.
The Herb Gardens of Chakra Phool, Jethimadh and Shimla Mirch grow herbs in every bed.
Typing a C in chat no longer opens Camera Mode in the Institute of Ocular Testing.
Notice the Unnoticeable, Legalize It and Four Letter Words wait for what started them in Glitch.
A shared street project's last card shows your share of the work.
Chat lines and the Community boards get a Thank you reaction.
Machines play their ready beep when a job is done, in Tiny Speck's own sounds.
The Still has its sounds: the hopper lid on Distill and its chime on Collect.
A potion's bottle uncorks, tips and pours when you quaff or pour it.
Your Scraper and Shovel are seen at work on Barnacles, Ice Nubbins, Dirt Piles and Peat.
Garden crops grow in minutes to an hour, and a plot shows how long is left.
Online, a Batterfly's hourly Guano is one pile on the street for everyone.
A Chicken you walk into says Squawk! and flies off.
Visitors see the owner's Magic Sticks, Piggy Feeder and Garden Gnomes on a home street.
A quoin's amount is larger and stays on screen long enough to read.
Make opens on your tools, grouped by kind, with search on both screens.
Leave a line with your Butler for visitors, and ask another player's Butler about its owner.
Click the favor display to see your favor with all eleven Giants.
Buddies show their faces in the Buddies list.
Speech bubbles stay with their speaker.
Oppidan Avenue's teleporters work, so nobody is shut in behind the beam.
Gold upgrade cards, such as Trade Channelling, can be bought in Firefox.
Firebog home streets and back yards stand their trees and huts on the ground.
A chat line holds 1,000 characters, as the original's did.
Another player's arrival is lighter and quicker on your screen.
Door keys lie on their streets again, in the spots the old wiki names.
Online a street has one key for everyone, back five minutes after it is picked up.
The street no longer stops for a moment when another player walks in.
The Cubimal card counts every figure you have found, as the Badges panel does.
Harbinger Heath's leftmost ladder has all its rungs.
Energy and mood go past 100 in the Paradise ticket streets.
Brillah Completist can be earned by visiting all 27 Brillah streets.
You can put your Mail Dispatcher away, and put it out again from Cultivate.
A street Piggy's name, captures, youth potions and Plops are shared with everyone online.
Sixteen more back yards look like players' 2012 pictures, and forest yards grow a real pine forest.
Set your own machine down in a Community Machine Room, and anyone there can use it.
Online, the Crown Game Teleporter takes 50 currants and joins you to a Game of Crowns.
Seven back yards look like players' own 2012 pictures of them, such as Night Lights and Torrid Cove.
Sharper on big screens: Party teleporters, Rook silhouettes, the Ball and the Giant icons.
A line typed in Local chat goes to Local, not to Global Chat.
Cubimal battles: set a figure down and it fights another player's figure nearby.
Street animals are in the same place for everyone online, from Piggies to Heli Kitties and Crabs.
Drag a pack item onto a thing in the world, like food onto a Piggy or a tool onto a rock.
Coral Caves and its yard Anemone Alley are drawn with their own pieces of the location art.
Louise Pasture Villa, an apartment hall, opens behind a new door on Louise Pasture.
Street Patches are shared online: everyone on a street tends, plants and grows the same Patch.
A tree grown on a street Patch is the same tree for everyone to pet, water and harvest.
One item picker for auctions, giving, wrapping gifts and the Butler's packages, with a search box.
Items from Dust Traps, gathering spots and dropped loot float up with their picture.
Trees and Chickens stand on the ground instead of floating above it.
Legalize It: nobody gets stuck in The Back Alley, and leaving the quest keeps your cards.
Wintry Place: /stuck takes you to the way out on the floor.
Pick up how many works on a shared street stack: take what you want, the rest stays for everyone.
Groddle Meadow, Groddle Forest and Alakol have redone map paintings, closer to the originals.
A garden left for hours comes back as far as it grew, a crop instead of dry shoots.
The ten public gardens are shared online: everyone on the street sees and tends the same plots.
